response.rationale: Both answers correctly express the stated sense of English “late.” Indonesian terlambat is standard for being late, while Malaysian Malay lewat is a standard and natural equivalent. The relation is a valid contrast between selected common forms, though it does not imply exclusivity: Malay also uses lambat/terlambat, and Indonesian has colloquial telat. No material false-friend problem is present; Indonesian lewat has other prominent meanings, so an explicit contrast could be pedagogically useful but is not required for correctness.
